[[File:Dessau, Anhaltische Gemäldegalerie, Johann Heinrich Beck, Odysseus bei Calypso am Meeresufer sitzend.jpg|thumb]]
In [[Greek mythology|Greek]] and [[Roman mythology]], '''[[w:Odysseus|Odysseus]]''' is a legendary [[Greeks|Greek]] king of [[w:Homeric Ithaca|Ithaca]] and the hero of [[Homer]]'s [[w:Epic poetry|epic poem]], the ''[[Odyssey]]''. 

{{theme-stub}}

== Quotes about {{PAGENAME}} ==

*[Odysseus was] tough, crafty, cheerful, of medium height, eloquent, and wise.
**In the account of [[w:Dares Phrygius|Dares the Phrygian]]  [[Dares Phrygius]], ''History of the Fall of Troy'' [https://www.theoi.com/Text/DaresPhrygius.html 13] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407120900/http://www.theoi.com/Text/DaresPhrygius.html |date=7 April 2023 }}

* [He was] shorter in truth by a head than Atreus’ son Agamemnon, / but broader, it would seem, in the chest and across the shoulders /... / Truly, to some deep-fleeced ram would I liken him / who makes his way through the great mass of the shining sheep-flocks.
** In Book III of [[Homer|Homer's]] [[Iliad]] [[Priam]]. {{Cite book |last=Homer |title=The Iliad of Homer |last2=Lattimore |first2=Richmond |last3=Martin |first3=Richard P. |date=2011 |publisher=University of Chicago Press |isbn=978-0-226-47048-1 |location=Chicago ; London |pages=Book III Lines 192-199}}

*In parts of their careers, Arjuna and Odysseus show similarities so numerous and detailed that they must be cognate figures, sharing an origin in the proto-hero of an oral proto-narrative.
**Nicholas Allen, 1998, quoted in: Elst K. in Udayanath Sahoo (editor), Shobha Rani Dash (editor) - Great Indian Epics, International Perspectives-Routledge (2021) 55-6
